title: [factory-setup-agent] Sandbox amendment: lint and coverage are now gate-enforced, offline, and self-evidencing
body:
Amendment for work item `wi_01M7YHSHX0QVJT6NMABZHQTT36`, answering two reports — builder `9ee7d48caa306084` and verifier `68041b41bb3232c8`. They describe one shortfall in two voices: the test and lint commands were not runnable as evidence from a role's agent container.

Deliverables are in `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/bsf/setup/`: `manifest.json` (validates, tier `renders`), the four `context/` documents, and `research-domains.txt`. No stubs (no third party), and no guardrails patch — skipped on an amendment.

## What changed

**The lint command is now enforced, not just documented.** The first amendment found the fix (`dotnet restore` before `dotnet format --verify-no-changes --no-restore`) but left it as prose in the runbook, so nothing made a role or a gate use it — and the verifier hit the same `CS0246` again. It is now `static_checks[0]`, `dotnet-format`, with a `jq` filter converting the formatter's JSON report to SARIF so the static gate counts findings per rule per file.

I reproduced the roles' failure exactly by moving `tests/Readings.Tests/obj/project.assets.json` aside, and confirmed restoring first recovers it. The check is proven in both directions: a scratch file raised five `WHITESPACE` findings and one `IDE0161` at the right lines, and the clean tree produces an empty SARIF. When `dotnet format` writes no report the command deliberately writes **no** SARIF, so a checker that did not run is reported unavailable rather than as a clean repo.

This matters more than it looks: `tests/Readings.Tests` sets neither `TreatWarningsAsErrors` nor `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild`, so the build says nothing about style in test code. `dotnet format` is the only thing that covers it.

**Coverage is measured, with no tool install and no network.** 86.9% of lines, four files. I first built this on the `dotnet-coverage` global tool and it worked — then `api.nuget.org` became unreachable from this container mid-episode and the install failed. That made the dependency concrete rather than theoretical, so I replaced it with the Code Coverage collector that already ships inside `Microsoft.CodeCoverage` (via `Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk`), reached with `--TestAdapterPath`. Same engine, same Cobertura, nothing installed, nothing added to the repo. The whole pipeline was then re-run offline to prove it.

**The test command got two more guards.** It globs `tests/*/bin/Debug/net*/*.Tests.dll` instead of naming one assembly, so a second test project runs without a manifest change, and it now fails on `outcome="Failed"` in the trx as well as on a zero count — so the verdict no longer rests on the runner's exit code alone. Both were checked against a real regression.

## Two things for a human, outside setup's remit

1. **`.factory/guardrails/coverage.json` still has `high_pct` and `floor_pct` at `0`** while coverage now reports 86.9%. `diff_min_pct` is 80 and will apply from the next PR. Worth a deliberate decision on the floor rather than leaving it at zero.
2. **`src/Readings/Program.cs` is 0 of 22 lines covered** — the only file with no covered line. A PR that only adds or changes a route will measure 0% diff coverage and fail gate 2. That is the gate telling the truth; the way through is `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing` and `WebApplicationFactory<Program>`, which `Program.cs` is already shaped for (`public partial class Program;`). It is a one-package product PR, not a coverage skip.

## Still unexplained

`dotnet test --no-build` exiting 0 having run nothing. Two role containers saw it; I could not reproduce it across nine conditions (non-TTY stdout, `TERM=dumb`, `CI=true`, `env -i` with only the sandbox's six base variables, missing `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, missing `project.assets.json`, and more) on the same SDK 11.0.100 and VSTest 18.12.0 the verifier names. Nothing the sandbox runs depends on `dotnet test` any more, so it is routed around rather than fixed, and it is recorded under `capabilities.not_exercised` and in the runbook's Traps table.

I declined the verifier's suggestion to pin an SDK with a `global.json`: it is a change to the repo, which setup does not make, and it would be a guess dressed as a fix given the failure never reproduced. The Traps table is the evidence if someone wants to take that decision deliberately.

## Verified here

Full pipeline under `env -i` with only the trial's six base variables plus the manifest's five, with every report directory deleted first and with `api.nuget.org` unreachable: install 0, build 0 warnings 0 errors, test 0 (nine passed, printed 9), control build and test both non-zero in an empty directory, coverage 0 with Cobertura parsed by the gate's own reader, static check 0 with a valid SARIF. Then the run command end to end, every route driven over HTTP including the new `GET /sensors/latest`, and a Chromium screenshot of `app_url`. Tier stays `renders`. Browser closed, app stopped, nothing listening on 5080, working tree clean.
